purpose: Owner-review draft: Dolbur's tier-2 click-through chapter (Sturdy mushroom, Clever mushroom, Lively mushroom), written in the reviewed Dolbur tier-1 chapter format - chapter-pilot-dolbur-t1.json is the same-traveler benchmark (pilot chapter-click-06). The chapter opens as soon as any material family reaches tier 2; the player picks one currently unlocked material inside the opening scene; the choice sets the route; Dolbur is dispatched around base camp; after the trip the player opens a click-through continuation carrying the journey's action, setbacks, decisions, and growth. Each route stands alone and holds the mandate the owner set for it: Life makes him earn both hook promises (the dinner and the dry camp) by bracing the failing awning first, Mana shows him testing whether the mushrooms' changing arrangement means something before the hidden spring is revealed, and Stamina makes the premature salting a real mistake he owns at once and repairs on screen. Dolbur's judgment grows behaviorally (survey first, test before believing, name the mistake by repairing it) without textual callbacks to a particular tier-1 route. Nothing here edits data/, source/, or the playable HTML.

presentationModel: Player opens a tier chapter when any material family reaches that tier. Inside the opening scene the player chooses one currently unlocked tier material; that choice determines the route. Dolbur is dispatched. When the trip finishes, the player opens a click-through continuation showing what happened around base camp and the route's outcome. Other unlocked routes can be played on later trips, one active route at a time.
playerFlow: op-01 -> op-02 -> choice -> confirm = byte-exact hook box for the chosen family -> one route departure box -> trip-start (dispatch, no result) -> trip timer -> trip-end (click to open the report) -> route return boxes in order, last box = byte-exact outcome. After the chapter, other unlocked choices remain available on later trips.

implementationNotes.chapterOpen: The chapter becomes available as soon as any material family reaches tier 2, per the engine's chapter gating (source/core.js expeditionChapter and unlockedExpeditionChapters, which open a chapter when a family's tier meets the chapter and filter routes to unlocked families). Suggested UI copy, outside the story beats: 'New chapter - Mushrooms at Base Camp.'
implementationNotes.optionGating: Show only options for material families currently unlocked at this tier; one, two, or three options are all valid states. The opening prose is written to hold when only one option exists.
implementationNotes.routeLock: The material choice sets the active route for this trip; other unlocked choices remain available on later trips, one active route at a time.
implementationNotes.tripTimer: The trip runs about two minutes on the game timer. The timer belongs to implementation and UI, not to story text.
implementationNotes.awardHandling: The script never states or implies that the player receives the chosen mushroom: the mushroom names which journey the telling follows, not freight. source/core.js settleExpedition (line 299) awards stamps, likeability, boost bundles, and bonuses only - no ingredient, no mushroom - and the trip-end beat only opens Dolbur's report; awarding belongs to the game's existing systems, outside story text.
implementationNotes.displayModel: Current in-game flow this script mirrors: the hook for the selected family already shows as the story preview before dispatch (source/app.js updateExpeditionStoryPreview text assignment at line 147, from the route preview in source/core.js), and the outcome shows once after the trip (source/core.js recordExpeditionStory; journal building at line 363). The confirm box repeats the hook, the final click-through beat repeats the outcome, and nothing pre-dispatch states outcome facts.

beatRules: Every beat carries id, phase, speaker, portrait, text. The choice beat additionally carries its note and its three option texts.

Narrator beats stay brief and set place, action, or a visible action. Dolbur carries the recognition, reasoning, and decisions in his own spoken lines; judgment growth comes through what he surveys, tests, orders, and repairs - never through mood labels. No route side character speaks: no accepted journey draft exists for Dolbur tier 2, so no dialogue is invented for the camp under the awning, the scouts, or the kitchen's background traffic; each side presence stays narrator-carried with one scene function.
Each return route opens with a 'The report starts...' narrator sentence so the post-trip account runs chronologically from where the trip went.

Each box is written to be comfortable in a dialogue box: about 40 words (whitespace token audit, hard ceiling 43 for every new beat). The byte-exact hook quote (confirm) and the byte-exact outcome quote (final return box) repeat already accepted screen text and are exempt from the target.

Portrait availability (verified): speaker 'narrator' is unvoiced scene text with no portrait. Speaker 'dolbur' shows the Dolbur portrait ('dolbur' - source/core.js TRAVELERS line 12 'DolburPortrait.png'; file assets/characters/DolburPortrait.webp). No other speaker beats exist: the camp, the scouts, and the kitchen background stay narrator-carried, so no 'none-new-side-character' beat appears in this chapter.

No outcome fact appears anywhere before the trip ends. Pre-dispatch boxes carry only hook facts and Dolbur's spoken intentions; the six shared units (op-01, op-02, choice text and note, trip-start, trip-end) carry no route-specific hook facts either, since the choice precedes the confirm.

Aftermath wording stays owned by the final byte-exact outcome beats (the outcome's 'crate-brace first, cook after' camp law with his name on the margin; the string pegged through the refused line and the spring reveal with the scouts' credit, 'and he lets them'; the premature salting owned at once, the re-rinse, the lid weighted with a stone, the double-surviving dinner, and the pot-lid stone entering the camp rulebook). Scene beats show the same journey facts in scene time in their own words; the ownership scan verifies zero outcome-phrase reuse in non-final beats.

Route independence: no beat assumes another route was seen, no cross-route characters or props except generic camp fixtures, no Neet-route assumptions, no Dolbur tier-1 references (the shortcut, decoy, splint, ropes, birds, timetable, and three-trip material stay inside their own accepted outcomes), no tier-3 or later references, and no customs recited outside the byte-exact outcome beats. Each of the three routes stands alone and reads cleanly in any play order.

Award discipline: no beat states or implies the player receives the chosen mushroom; the trip's rewards belong to the game's existing settlement systems outside story text (source/core.js settleExpedition).

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The mushroom assignments are stacked on the camp table this morning, and the mushroom work is Dolbur's.

beats.speaker: dolbur
beats.text: Pio! Camp day! Belt, boots, and rations, all checked by hand this morning. Point me at the mushrooms, and I will make the assignment worth retelling.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Choose which mushroom sends Dolbur out.
beats.note: Only options whose material family is unlocked at this tier are shown. The opening prose above is written to hold whether one option or three are available. The chosen mushroom names the journey this telling follows; it is the story's focus, never a settlement award.

options.teaser: Storm season arrived early, the old awning is crabby, and one promise covers dinner and the evening's weather.
The camp mushrooms redraw themselves every dawn, and the scouts want to know if the moving means anything.
A pan of lively mushrooms, one salt cellar, and a dinner where timing beats seasoning.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: Dolbur takes the assignment and gets to it; whatever happens out there comes home with him.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: The trip is over. Open Dolbur's report to see what happened, and how it ended.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: Storm season is early and the base camp awning is older than everyone standing under it. Dolbur has promised the camp a mushroom dinner and a dry night.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: Sturdy mushrooms, then! Storm's coming early, the awning is older than everyone it shelters, and I promised the camp the evening meal and the weather. Both will behave by suppertime - the storm is invited to watch me keep them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts under the old awning: the season's first wet gust ran through camp, the canvas swung, the frame groaned at its joints, and beneath that roof sat the cookfire, the pot, and both of the evening's promises.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: That roof is one shove from a wiped-out supper. Weight speaks before fire does tonight: the cargo crates to me, the lot, and the pot's clock keeps running. Both promises get kept in one piece.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The crates piled in two deep: wedged under the long frame at the sagging corner, boxed around the middle pole's feet, and walked along row by row with a shove until the canvas stopped swinging and stood still over the fire.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The pot kept its hour: caps checked one basket at a time, then in, exactly on the camp's evening clock. The fix asked the dinner for nothing - that was the point of doing the roof in daylight.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The storm arrived after lamps with its better push: gusts leaned on the canvas line, water sheeted off the awning, and the crates answered every shove - flame straight, boots dry, camp dry under its old roof.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Dinner ran the tables: bowls emptied, seconds went around, and the camp counted its kept promises on two fingers - fed, and dry, with the cookfire's light still leaning on the crates.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: By next morning the working order hung painted over the cookfire arch - weight before fire, crates before pots - with his belt tally signed underneath as the author.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He props the frame on sturdy crates and gets the caps into the pot on schedule. The awning holds, 'crate-brace first, cook after' is camp law with his name on the margin, and dinner is good.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: Base camp's clever mushrooms rearrange themselves every dawn, and the scouts want to know whether the arrangement means anything. Dolbur treats the question seriously.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: The clever patch, then! It moves house every dawn and the scouts want the meaning. I take that question personally: dawn to dawn, mark by mark, and their theories stand a test. Two dawns of eyes beat one dawn of guessing.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the mushroom patch at first light: half the caps stood somewhere new to every eye in camp, and the scouts had theories before the mist burned off - wind, ground, or a good week coming.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: Fine question, worth a real test: every cap gets marked where it stands tonight and again at tomorrow's dawn, and whatever holds its ground across both dawns gets its own look. Guesses are for card tables. Patches get tested.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Chalked rings went down around every cap before dark. By next dawn the patch had shifted its majority again, fresh caps upright in the gaps, and one strip of dirt stood exactly as bare as the evening before.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Dawn two moved everything else and the strip none. Laid side by side, the dawn maps agreed: the bare strip ran straight as a fence rail from the patch's near corner out past the drying racks.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Wind's theory collapsed first: a shoving gust leaves no ruler-straight, always-bare lane behind. Twice bare and dead straight, the strip read as a decision, and decisions come from somewhere. The patch had started answering back.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The only instrument the scouts never brought was a straight edge, so he brought the straight: cord over shoulder, stakes in hand, and the whole camp of theories parked at the patch's edge waiting on a walking test.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He pegs a string through the line they keep refusing, and the string-line traces to a spring nobody knew was close. The scouts credit the mushrooms, and he lets them.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: Dinner is lively mushrooms in the pan, which means timing matters and checking matters more. Dolbur has one job and one salt cellar.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: Lively mushrooms, then! One pan, one salt cellar, and a dinner that will not sit still. The rule tonight: eyes first, salt second, checking before anything touches a hot pan. I have been rehearsing my patient face all week.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the kitchen corner: pan singing, one salt cellar riding his belt, the lively caps going in like dice. He knew pans, said the hour, and the salt went in ahead of any checking at all.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Salted too young, the caps surrendered their water early and turned tight and shy in a pan ready to glorify them. The sizzle died to a hiss, and the kitchen smelled like an evening backing out of its own promise.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: Stop. That was my hand - salt before eyes, confidence before checking. The caps and the pan did nothing wrong; the mistake is mine in full. The batch goes to the wash, and the salt cellar gets exiled to the far counter.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The salted batch went into clean water before the pan had stopped complaining, and came out honest again - not the evening's proudest serving, but a true one, and the camp's long tables took it without complaint.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Batch two ran by the book: caps checked one by one before the salt got anywhere near. Then the pan opened its second act - the liveliest caps leaping the rim, and the loose lid bouncing like it wanted to join them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: A hearth stone came down square on the lid and the performance stopped mid-air. The pan kept its cargo, the second batch cooked out clean, and the tables would never know how close it ran.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The stone stayed on post after the washing-up, holding the lid out of habit, and Dolbur told its story to anyone parked near the fire until the fire banked itself. A stone cannot blush; he pretended not to notice.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He salts the pan before checking whether they are ready - his documented way to lose dinner. He owns it at once, re-rinses, weights the lid with a stone, and dinner survives twice; the pot-lid stone is glued into the camp rulebook's margin as a lesson.

skillStages.planning: planning.md outputs restated for the Dolbur tier-2 chapter: the reviewed tier-1 chapter shape (opening -> choice -> hook confirm -> departure -> dispatch -> return beats -> outcome), with the same documented deviation - no accepted journey draft exists for Dolbur tier 2, so the continuation between hook and outcome is planned as new fan-written scene work to each outcome's own action order. POV limits: pre-dispatch boxes may state hook facts and Dolbur's spoken intentions only - no result - and the six shared units carry no route-specific facts since the choice precedes the confirm. The owner's three route mandates drive the beat orders: Life earns both hook promises through the failing awning (bracing first, cooking second, storm third), Mana tests the rearranging before revealing, and Stamina stages the premature salting as a real mistake owned and repaired with the stone caused on screen.
skillStages.drafting: dialogue-and-behavior.md governs the boxes: Dolbur's lines are energetic and direct (established anchor: 'An energetic warrior who approaches adventures with plenty of enthusiasm'; the job description's 'another energetic adventure, checking the route before setting out'), and the growth shows as conduct - a survey before the pot, a two-dawn test before a belief, an apology that arrives as a repair order. No side-character dialogue invented: the camp eats and gets rained on in body, the scouts trail and hold theories without speaking, the kitchen background stays background. The end of each route is the accepted outcome beat, so each route ends with the pack's own claim. Dolbur's 'Pio!' salute in op-02 uses the established expedition greeting register (source/app.js profile index 1) with plain ASCII punctuation.
skillStages.reviewing: revision-checklist pass on all three click-throughs: choice causality (the mushroom names the route; no theme confusion), no pre-dispatch outcome disclosure, route independence (no cross-route characters or props beyond generic camp fixtures, no Neet-route assumptions, no tier-1 or later custom recitations outside the byte-exact outcomes), character anchoring (the camp as beneficiaries, the scouts as questioners with one function, the kitchen as background), voice consistency in every spoken box, box economy, and mapping completeness (each outcome's action order shows fully in the scene before the final quote).

characterNotes.dolbur: Tier-2 Dolbur is the established warrior two habits deep: energetic, direct, and now treating checks as a matter of course - he surveys the roof before the pot (Life), builds a test before believing a theory (Mana), and converts his own mistake into a repair order within one spoken line (Stamina). The growth is behavioral because the campaign cannot assume the player saw a Dolbur tier-1 route: no outcome or scene references what any earlier telling established. His tier-3..5 material is not referenced. Portrait: 'dolbur' (verified: source/core.js TRAVELERS line 12 'DolburPortrait.png'; file assets/characters/DolburPortrait.webp).
characterNotes.campCompanions: Life route only, unnamed: the camp under the awning - the beneficiaries of both hook promises (fed and dry). They count their blessings in body language and wait out the storm under the braced roof. No speaker beats, no portrait; narrator-carried.
characterNotes.scouts: Mana route only, unnamed: the camp's scouts who want the rearranging to mean something. They supply the morning theories (wind, ground, a good week) that the test is set against, and stay with the question to the end. No speaker beats, no portrait; narrator-carried.
characterNotes.kitchenBackground: Stamina route only, unnamed: the kitchen corner's traffic and the long tables who eat the rescued dinner without ever learning how close it ran. No speaker beats, no portrait; narrator-carried.

continuityFlags: No accepted journey draft exists for Dolbur tier 2 (the journey-pilot files cover Neet t1 and t2 only). All beats between hook and outcome are new fan-written scene work staged to each outcome's own action order; the owner may want a companion journey-pilot-dolbur-t2 before v2 integration. Hooks and outcomes are the only protected texts.

Shared-unit spoiler discipline: op-01, op-02, the choice text and note, and the two dispatch lines carry no route-specific hook or outcome facts; per-route hook facts appear only in each route's own option teaser, byte-exact hook, and departure line. Per-option teasers restate hook facts in fresh wording, as in the reviewed tier-1 benchmark.

Scene-versus-outcome wording split: the beats show the outcomes' journey facts in scene time (the crate bracing and the storm held; the two-dawn test and the bare straight strip; the salted-first evening, the wash, the leaping caps, and the stone) but in their own words; each phrase the outcome uses as its standing claim ('props the frame on sturdy crates', 'The awning holds', 'crate-brace first, cook after', camp law with his name on the margin; 'pegs a string', 'the line they keep refusing', the spring nobody knew was close, 'The scouts credit the mushrooms', 'he lets them'; the documented way to lose dinner, owning it at once, re-rinses, 'weights the lid with a stone', 'dinner survives twice', the pot-lid stone entering the camp rulebook) is verified to appear only in the byte-exact outcome beats.

Route independence verified by scan: no traveler names other than Dolbur; crates, canvas, and the cookfire arch exist only in Life, the scouts, patch marks, and the straight strip only in Mana, the pan, salt cellar, and hearth stone only in Stamina; no Neet-route assumptions; no Dolbur tier-1 vocabulary outside those accepted outcomes (no shortcut, decoy, splint, ropes, birds, timetable, or three-trip material); the judgment growth is behavioral only (survey first, test first, own-and-repair) with no textual callbacks to any earlier route.

Later-tier and earlier-tier borrow guards: the crate-brace is not the tier-3 orchard gate motto and never says 'unload'; the bearing-walk along the bare strip is generic straight-line tooling, not the tier-4 fork-cord custom, and no cave, feather, or nest material is referenced; the hearth stone is a lid weight caused on screen, not the tier-4 distance-stone custom; the patch, canvas, and cookfire are generic camp fixtures rather than borrowings from the tier-1 patch defense. The tier-5 campaign material is not referenced.

Pre-dispatch content (opening, teasers, hooks, departures, dispatch lines) is safe for the current display model: hook facts and declared intentions only.
